items.claim: The antithetic single-proverb boundary at 21:29 is well-formed, isolated cleanly from both neighbors, and its two ketiv/qere notes are accurately counted.
items.evidence: Skeleton comparison shows Prov.21.28 and Prov.21.30 share no content token with 21:29 beyond the generic noun איש (man), which recurs too broadly in the book to carry cohesion weight; pmarks_Prov.json kq confirms exactly 2 notes at Prov.21.29, matching the row's count: ketiv יכין / qere יָבִ֬ין on the verb, and ketiv דרכיו / qere דַּרְכּֽוֹ on the suffixed noun the row calls 'the pronoun.' 21:30-31 instead pair with each other via the shared יהוה frame ("no wisdom against Yahweh" / "victory is with Yahweh"), confirming 21:29 sits alone between two different micro-units rather than opening either.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at 22:4 is correctly isolated, and the rejected 22:5 rival is the genuinely adjacent candidate rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: Skeleton comparison: Prov.22.3 and Prov.22.5 share zero content tokens with 22:4; the synthetic result-formula reading (humility/fear-of-Yahweh -> wealth/honor/life) is self-contained within the verse. 22:3 (danger-avoidance) and 22:5 (path-of-the-wicked) are also topically unconnected to 22:4, so no undisclosed cross-seam cohesion straddles either boundary.

items.claim: The single-proverb boundary at 22:11 is well-isolated on both sides and its single ketiv/qere note is correctly counted against the inventory.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq lists exactly 1 note at Prov.22.11, matching the row's singular claim. Skeleton check shows Prov.22.10 and Prov.22.12 share no content token with 22:11, so isolation holds on both sides even though the row's rejected_alternative argues only the 22:12 rival (the eyes-of-Yahweh saying).

items.claim: The 5-verse prologue span, its seam on both sides, and the shalishim ketiv/qere crux are all sound, but device_notes overstates the internal grammar as 'one periodic sentence' when the bytes show two distinct governing clauses, and one cited ref (23:1) is never argued in the prose.
items.evidence: v.20 opens with הֲלֹ֤א כָתַ֣בְתִּי לְ֭ךָ ("have I not written to you"), an interrogative-perfect main clause, not a continuation of v.17's imperative chain (הַ֥ט ... וּ֭שְׁמַע); v.21's two purpose infinitives, לְהוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֗ and לְהָשִׁ֥יב, grammatically attach to v.20's כתבתי ("I have written"), not to v.17's imperative, so the passage is better described as two linked persuasive moves (vv.17-19 imperative+purpose; vv.20-21 rhetorical-question+purpose) unified by address function rather than one continuous grammatical period. Separately, the row also cites Prov.23.1 among its supporting verse references without ever arguing that verse in the prose, an unexplained citation. On the core claims: skeleton check confirms 22:16 and 22:17 share no token (clean C2|C3 seam) and 22:21/22:22 share none either; pmarks_Prov.json marks confirms PE at Prov.22.21 exactly as cited; the crux itself is byte-accurate -- ketiv שלשום against qere שָׁלִישִׁ֑ים at Prov.22.20, matching pmarks kq (1 note) and correctly reported as unresolved.

items.claim: The 22:22-23 admonition_unit is cleanly bounded on both sides and correctly names the prologue as the strongest rival for merger.
items.evidence: Skeleton check: Prov.22.21 shares no content token with 22:22 (אַֽל תִּגְזָל ...), and 22:23 shares none with 22:24; the PE at Prov.22.21 the row cites as the prologue's close is confirmed in pmarks_Prov.json marks.

items.claim: The 22:24-25 admonition_unit boundary and its single ketiv/qere disclosure at 22:25 are both accurate.
items.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq lists exactly 1 note at Prov.22.25, matching ketiv ארחתו / qere אֹֽרְחֹתָ֑יו as cited. Skeleton check confirms 22:23/22:24 (אַל תִּ֭תְרַע ...) share no token and 22:25/22:26 share no token, supporting clean isolation on both sides of the pair.

items.claim: The 22:26-27 admonition_unit is correctly bounded and its rejected_alternative addresses the genuine risk of over-atomizing v.27 rather than a strawman.
items.evidence: v.27's rhetorical question has no independent referent for 'he' or the pledge scenario without v.26 (אַל תְּהִ֥י ...), confirming the two verses are grammatically dependent. Skeleton check shows 22:25/22:26 and 22:27/22:28 (אַל תַּ֭סֵּג ...) share no tokens, so the pair is cleanly isolated from its neighbors on both sides.

items.claim: unit_type single_proverb misclassifies 22:28: its negative imperative matches this cluster's own admonition_unit pattern rather than the declarative-sentence pattern this cluster's C2 single_proverb rows exemplify, and the book strategy grants the single_proverb option to C4, not explicitly to C3.
items.evidence: 22:28 opens with the negative imperative אַל תַּ֭סֵּג ("do not move"), grammatically the same kind of opener as the immediately preceding admonition_unit rows in this cluster (אַֽל תִּגְזָל 22:22; אַל תִּ֭תְרַע 22:24; אַל תְּהִ֥י 22:26), whereas this cluster's own C2 single_proverb rows (21:29, 22:4, 22:11) are all declarative sentences with no imperative verb. The owner-ruled granularity policy names admonition_unit as C3's operative category and grants the single_proverb option explicitly only to C4 ("admonition_unit/single_proverb per bytes"), with no equivalent grant for C3. Absence of a motive clause is rhetorical brevity, not a change of grammatical mood; a bare imperative-plus-relative-clause maxim is still structurally admonition-shaped. The span itself is sound -- skeleton check confirms 22:27/22:28 and 22:28/22:29 share no token -- and the non-adjacent recurrence the row cites at 23:10-11 is byte-confirmed: Prov.23.10 opens with the identical clause אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם (22:28's own opening is אַל תַּ֭סֵּג גְּב֣וּל עוֹלָ֑ם), this time followed by a motive.
